title: Palaeoproteomic evidence for late Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus in mainland East Asia
projectDescription: Hominin fossil and genetic evidence indicate that several hominin populations occupied East and Southeast Asia during the Middle and Late Pleistocene. Despite the existence of well-documented hominin fossil collections north of 25°N latitude and south of 7°S latitude, on Java, H. erectus fossils remain scarce in southern China and mainland Southeast Asia. This submission contains palaeoproteomic data of five fauna specimens from Naxian Cave, three hominin specimens from Naxian Cave, and two hominin specimens from Baxian Cave. These two sites  are dated to the Late Middle Pleistocene and located in, in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, southern China. Palaeoproteomic analysis reveals the presence of an endogenous dental proteome in all five hominin teeth studied molecularly and indicates that four of the teeth derive from male individuals. Four specimens represent a hominin population previously unsampled using genetic or proteomic methods, providing novel information on the spatiotemporal distribution of H. erectus in the Pleistocene of East Asia.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Dental enamel proteins were extracted by demineralisation and immediate solubilization of protein fragments into 5% HCl for the Naxian hominins, 10% TFA for the Naxian fauna, and acid etching using 5% HCl for the Baxian hominins. For the Naxian fauna, dentine was extracted using demineralisation in EDTA, with in-solution using trypsin. For the baxian hominin dentine, demineralisation was conducted using 0.6 M HCl followed by buffer transfer and MWCO ultrafiltering, into separate sub-extracts, into ammonium-bicarbonate buffer, with subsequent digestion with trypsin. Faunal extracts from Naxian Cave were separated on an EASY-nLC 1200 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled to a Exploris 480 Orbitrap mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Hominin dental enamel extracts from Naxian Cave were analysed on a Vanquish Neo UPLC (Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled to a Exploris 480 Orbitrap mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Both the dentine and the dental enamel extracts from Baxian Cave were analysed on an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled to an Easy n-LC 1200 HPLC system (Thermo Fisher Scientific) over a 120 minute gradient. Blank extractions were included in all cases to monitor the existence of exogenous contaminants during the procedure.
dataProcessingProtocol: The raw data was analysed using MaxQuant, pFind, and PEAKS in parallel, with searches performed separately for sites and skeletal tissues. Variations on the same search strategy were used for each protein software, including PTMs selection aimed at recovering peptides carrying diagenetically-derived PTMs, the allowance of a high number of variable PTMs per peptide, no fixed modifications, unspecific peptide cleavage settings, and short to long peptide length tolerances. For the hominin dental enamel, a database was used containing the most common dental enamel proteins as well as protein sequences for all living great apes, protein sequences reconstructed to have existed at the ancestral nodes of the living great apes, those translated from available archaic hominins, as well as protein sequences determined proteomically for previously analysed hominins. For hominin dentine, the complete human reference proteome was used, with to it added the reference proteomes translated from high-coverage Neanderthal and Denisovan genomes, as well as uniquely derived protein sequences from Xiahe 1 and the Penghu hominin mandibles. Initial statistical analyses and data visualization were conducted in R, with subsequent ancient protein sequence reconstruction and phylogenetic analysis conducted separately for the three protein data analysis strategies employed.
